headline: Renewed Iran strikes rattle futures as August's rally holds firm
body: Combat between the U.S. and Iran resumed overnight after weeks of calm, with American forces striking Iranian rocket launchers reportedly positioned to mine the Strait of Hormuz. Crude jumped on the news, with Brent pushing above ninety dollars a barrel and WTI near eighty-six, while U.S. equity futures slipped only modestly, Dow futures off about a tenth of a percent and Nasdaq futures closer to flat. The pullback reads as a wobble rather than a rout: the Dow is still up roughly two percent this month and on pace for a fifth straight monthly advance, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq are tracking their first monthly gains since May, up around three and four percent. Layered on top is a Fed repricing, as Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks cut September rate-cut odds to roughly a third, with some traders now pricing in hike risk, capping the rally's room to extend.

The CNN Fear & Greed gauge sits at 54, squarely neutral and down a few points from recent readings, consistent with a market absorbing a geopolitical shock without tipping into panic. Energy has been the clearest beneficiary of the Hormuz tensions, with major producers and tanker operators posting some of the market's largest year-to-date gains as the supply-disruption trade stays intact. Retail chatter offers less of a clean signal today: WallStreetBets mention trackers still show AI-adjacent names like Nvidia and Alphabet dominating attention with a bullish tilt, alongside a sharp, fast spike in Oracle mentions that looks more like momentum-chasing than any coordinated fear or euphoria. On balance, today's read leans more on overnight headlines and price action than on any distinct social-sentiment extreme.
